Summary Executive Summary & Abstract

Key Takeaway in Simple Words

BloodNet+ is an easy-to-use web platform that saves lives during medical emergencies. Instead of making panicked phone calls or posting on WhatsApp, a patient simply puts in their blood requirement. The system instantly alerts nearby voluntary donors and verified hospital blood banks on their phones in seconds, gives exact turn-by-turn driving directions to the hospital, and awards an official verified certificate with a scannable QR code.

1. The Real-Life Problem

In medical emergencies like car accidents, surgeries, and cancer treatments, patients need blood urgently—often within 60 minutes (the "Golden Hour"). Today, families face massive problems:

  • They have to make dozens of phone calls to friends, relatives, and static hospital directories.
  • Up to 70% of numbers in old registries are switched off, wrong, or out of town.
  • WhatsApp and Facebook blood requests spread slowly, contain outdated information, and attract online scammers.
  • Hospitals keep their blood bank inventory on private computers, so patients do not know which hospital has the required blood unit available right now.

2. What We Built (BloodNet+)

We designed and implemented BloodNet+, a real-time web application built with the MERN stack (MongoDB, Express, React, Node.js) and Socket.IO WebSockets. It acts as an intelligent, automated bridge connecting three main groups:

1. Patients / Recipients

Can request blood in under 30 seconds with blood group, units, hospital location, and urgency level.

2. Voluntary Donors

Receive instant notifications on their screen showing how far away the hospital is, and can accept with 1 click.

3. Hospital Blood Banks

Can update their 8-group stock in real time, fulfill requests directly, and view critical low-stock alerts.

3. Key Results & Achievements

The platform is fully implemented, tested, and deployed live on cloud infrastructure (Render.com) with MongoDB Atlas:

  • Instant Matching: Sub-second proximity calculation using the Haversine mathematical formula.
  • Fast Alerts: Real-time push notification delivered to active donors in less than 180 milliseconds.
  • Safe Routing: Direct turn-by-turn Google Maps navigation to verified street destinations.
  • Tamper-Proof Recognition: Dynamic SHA-256 scannable QR certificates to encourage voluntary donors to donate again.
  • Zero Privacy Leakage: Donor phone numbers and exact live coordinates are strictly shielded until mutual agreement.

Chapter 1 Introduction

1.1 Background & Motivation

Blood is a vital healthcare resource that cannot be artificially manufactured; it only comes from generous human donors. According to medical statistics in India, there is an annual shortfall of over 1 million units of blood. However, the biggest bottleneck is not just the total amount of blood—it is time and connectivity.

When an emergency happens, every minute lost searching for a donor increases the risk of organ failure or death. This crucial first hour after traumatic injury is known worldwide as the "Golden Hour". If blood can be delivered within this window, patient survival rates increase dramatically.

The Core Question

How can technology cut down blood procurement time from 4 to 12 hours down to just a few minutes, without compromising patient privacy or donor safety?

1.2 Project Overview

BloodNet+ is a modern web application designed from the ground up to solve this communication gap. It is built to be fast, reliable, accessible on any smartphone or computer without installing heavy apps, and extremely simple to understand.

Who Uses BloodNet+?

Recipient / Patient

Creates emergency or scheduled blood requests. Tracks donor responses live on a clean dashboard.

Voluntary Donor

Receives live alerts for nearby compatible requests. Views road distance, accepts, and gets directions.

Hospital Staff

Manages live inventory of 8 blood groups (A+, B+, O+, AB+, etc.). Verifies completed donations and issues certificates.

Chapter 2 Problem Statement & Existing Systems

2.1 The Problem with Existing Methods

Before building BloodNet+, we studied the existing ways people try to get blood during emergencies. Every current method has severe flaws:

Existing Method How It Currently Works Why It Fails During Emergencies
Manual Phone Calling Family members call relatives, friends, and old paper blood-donor lists one by one. Extremely slow (takes 4–8 hours). Over 70% of numbers are switched off, wrong, or people have moved.
WhatsApp & Facebook Posts A message is copied and pasted into multiple group chats asking for donors. Zero verification. Fake phone numbers spread rapidly. Messages linger for weeks after the patient is already treated.
Government Portals (e.g. e-RaktKosh) Shows static numbers of units reported by major government blood banks. Static snapshot view. Does not notify active donors in the street, provides no live transit routing, and updates slowly.
Hospital Standalone ERPs Hospitals use private software to log their internal blood bags for billing. Completely closed systems. Families have to physically travel between hospitals to check if blood is available.
BloodNet+ (Our Platform) Automated web platform with live push dispatch, GPS distance, routing, and hospital inventory. Sub-second donor matching, live routing, transparent stock, and scannable digital certification.

2.2 The Three Main Bottlenecks

1. Critical Time Loss

Manual calls waste precious hours while patients bleed or await urgent surgery in the ICU.

2. Inactive & Dead Contacts

Static donor registries contain old phone numbers of people who are no longer available to donate.

3. Navigation Dead-Ends

Raw GPS pins often point to the wrong hospital gate or alleyway; verified street addresses are essential for quick arrival.

Chapter 3 Project Objectives

Primary Goal

To design and develop an open, high-speed, automated emergency blood donation network that connects recipients with the closest eligible donors and hospital blood banks in under one minute.

Specific Engineering Goals

  • 1. Build Fast Multi-Role Web Portals: Create clean, responsive web interfaces for Recipients, Donors, Hospitals, and Administrators that work seamlessly on both mobile phones and laptops.
  • 2. Implement Sub-Second Proximity Matching: Use GPS coordinates and the mathematical Haversine formula to instantly sort and filter donors by distance from the patient's hospital.
  • 3. Live Instant Alerts via WebSockets: Establish persistent Socket.IO connections so compatible donors receive request alerts on their screen immediately (under 180 ms latency) without reloading the webpage.
  • 4. Address-First Turn-by-Turn Navigation: Integrate verified destination street addresses and Google Maps navigation to eliminate transit delays and ensure donors arrive at the correct hospital entrance.
  • 5. Transparent Hospital Blood Bank Management: Provide hospital staff with a live dashboard to update inventory for all 8 blood groups (A+, A-, B+, B-, AB+, AB-, O+, O-) with automatic low-stock warning banners.
  • 6. Tamper-Proof Digital Recognition (QR Certificate): Automatically award verifiable certificates with SHA-256 cryptographic hashes and scannable QR codes to recognize and retain voluntary donors.
  • 7. Strong Privacy Protection: Ensure no personal donor phone numbers or exact live locations are shared publicly until both recipient and donor mutually accept the match.

Chapter 4 How BloodNet+ Works

4.1 The 3-Tier System Architecture

BloodNet+ follows a clean, decoupled 3-tier architecture that ensures high speed, security, and scalability:

Layer Technologies What It Does (In Simple Words)
1. Frontend (Client Layer) React 18, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, Vite Runs in the user's web browser. Displays buttons, live maps, donor cards, and forms smoothly without page freezes.
2. Backend (API & Engine) Node.js, Express.js, Socket.IO The central brain. Receives blood requests, calculates distances, checks security tokens, and broadcasts live alerts.
3. Database & Cloud MongoDB Atlas, Render Cloud, GitHub Actions Stores user profiles, blood stock numbers, and completed donation audit logs securely in the cloud with 99.9% uptime.

4.2 The 6-Step Emergency Lifecycle

The entire emergency flow from start to finish is completed in 6 simple, automated steps:

Step 1: Emergency Request

The patient or family selects blood group, units needed, and hospital location in <30 seconds.

Step 2: Proximity Calculation

The backend runs the Haversine formula to identify compatible donors within traveling distance.

Step 3: Instant Push Alert

Socket.IO sends a real-time alert directly to nearby donors' dashboards in <180 milliseconds.

Step 4: Donor Acceptance

An available donor clicks "Accept & Donate". Contact details activate under mutual consent.

Step 5: Turn-by-Turn Navigation

1-click opens Google Maps with the exact street destination, showing real-time traffic and ETA.

Step 6: Verified Certificate

Hospital marks the donation as fulfilled. System instantly generates a tamper-proof SHA-256 QR certificate.

Figure 4.1: Address-First Google Maps Navigation — Real-Time Highway Transit Routing

Chapter 5 Core Modules & Features

5.1 Patient / Recipient Module

Designed for people in stressful situations. The interface is clean, free of clutter, and requires only 3 essential inputs: Blood Group, Hospital Location, and Urgency Level (Normal vs Urgent). Once submitted, the screen updates in real time to show which donors or hospitals have responded.

5.2 Voluntary Donor Module

Allows healthy citizens to register their blood group and receive alerts when someone nearby is in critical need. Features include:

  • Distance Indicator: Shows exactly how far away the hospital is (e.g., "~1.1 km away").
  • One-Click Acceptance: Donors can accept immediately with a single button click.
  • Location Privacy: Donors only share their travel coordination when they explicitly choose to accept.

5.3 Hospital Blood Bank Management

Hospitals have special access to manage their physical blood stock across all 8 standard blood groups. Key capabilities:

  • Real-Time Stock Counter: Staff can increment or decrement unit counts with + and - buttons.
  • Critical Depletion Warnings: If stock for any group drops below the safety threshold (5 units), the system flashes an urgent red banner (e.g., "Critical Stock Alert: B- and AB- need attention").
  • Atomic Inventory Reservations: Prevents two patients from claiming the same blood bag at the same time.
Figure 5.1: Hospital Blood Bank Dashboard with 8-group stock matrix and critical depletion warnings

5.4 Verified Donor Certification

To motivate voluntary donors and retain them for future emergencies, BloodNet+ includes a built-in digital certificate generator:

  • Generates an official certificate featuring the donor's name, blood group, date, and hospital name.
  • Includes a unique SHA-256 cryptographic verification hash.
  • Features a scannable QR code that anyone can scan with a phone camera to verify that the certificate is authentic and not faked.
Figure 5.2: Official Verified Donor Certificate with SHA-256 Hash and QR Verification

Chapter 6 Technologies Used & Why

Every technology in BloodNet+ was deliberately chosen to provide speed, reliability, and zero cost during deployment:

Technology Category Why We Chose It (Simple Explanation)
React 18 Frontend Framework Allows building fast, interactive dashboards where parts of the page update instantly without refreshing the entire screen.
Tailwind CSS 3 UI Styling Provides clean, responsive design that works beautifully on any mobile phone, tablet, or desktop monitor.
Node.js & Express Backend API Lightweight and handles hundreds of simultaneous requests without lagging. Built with JavaScript for end-to-end consistency.
Socket.IO Real-Time Engine Enables instant two-way communication between server and browser, pushing alerts to donors in less than 180 milliseconds.
MongoDB Atlas Cloud Database Fast, flexible NoSQL cloud database that easily handles geospatial queries and stores blood stock records safely.
Google Maps API Navigation Provides world-class turn-by-turn driving directions to street addresses, avoiding dead-end alleyways.
Render.com Cloud Hosting Reliable containerized hosting platform with automated continuous deployment (CI/CD) and free SSL HTTPS encryption.
SHA-256 + QR Security Industry-standard cryptographic algorithm that guarantees digital certificates cannot be altered or forged.

Chapter 8 Advantages & Real-World Impact

8.1 Key Advantages Over Old Systems

1. Saves the Critical "Golden Hour"

Replaces 4 to 8 hours of desperate manual calling with automated sub-second proximity dispatch.

2. Address-First Transit Guidance

Guides donors directly to the exact hospital gate using Google Maps, eliminating wasted travel time.

3. Transparent Hospital Blood Stock

Families can immediately check which hospital has the required units in stock before traveling.

4. Motivates Repeat Donors

Official cryptographic QR certificates recognize community donors and encourage regular voluntary donation.

8.2 Privacy & Security Protections

  • No Public Phone Number Dumps: Personal phone numbers are never displayed on public pages; they are revealed only after both parties agree to coordinate.
  • Automated 24-Hour Expiry: All location sharing and coordination channels automatically lock after 24 hours to protect user privacy.
  • Atomic Transactions: Prevents race conditions where two patients might accidentally claim the same last blood unit.

8.3 Limitations of Current Version

While BloodNet+ solves the core emergency communication problem, like all software systems it has some current constraints:

  • Internet Dependency: Requires active mobile data or Wi-Fi connectivity to receive real-time push alerts.
  • Donor Community Size: In remote rural areas, response times depend on how many voluntary donors in that specific village are registered.

Chapter 9 Future Scope & Conclusion

9.1 Future Scope (What Can Be Added Next)

BloodNet+ has a modular architecture that makes it easy to add advanced features in future versions:

1. AI Blood Shortage Forecasting

Using Machine Learning models to predict seasonal shortages (e.g. dengue outbreaks or summer dips) weeks in advance.

2. IoT Smart Cold-Chain Tracking

Placing temperature and GPS sensor tags inside blood transport boxes to monitor blood temperature during transit.

3. National Portal Interoperability

Connecting with the government's central e-RaktKosh portal via standardized REST APIs for national synchronization.

4. Dedicated Mobile Apps with SMS Fallback

Building React Native mobile apps with automated offline SMS alerts for rural areas with weak 4G internet.

9.2 Conclusion

Final Verdict

BloodNet+ successfully achieves its mission to bridge the emergency blood procurement gap through technology. By replacing panic-driven manual calling with automated real-time matching, live street navigation, transparent hospital inventory, and tamper-proof digital certificates, BloodNet+ provides a fast, humane, and dependable platform that can genuinely save human lives during critical medical emergencies.
